card.name: Right before a prohibition like cannot or not
card.fires_on: The word or mark just before a negated verb such as cannot, should not or do not, mostly in drug-combination warnings. It also fires on a subject, comma or 'for example' when a prohibition is expected next.

modes.label: Should not be combined
modes.description: The word 'not' after 'should' in statements that two drugs must not be given together.

modes.label: Lead-in to a prohibition
modes.description: A comma, subject or 'doses' just before an expected 'do not' or 'cannot' clause.
modes.example: In addition<<,>> do not start escitalopram tablets

modes.label: Cannot in general prose
modes.description: The word 'cannot' or a subject before 'couldn't' in an argument or quotation.
modes.example: "A house divided against itself<< cannot>> stand"

card.writes: It pushes the model toward writing cannot, not allowed or must not as the next word.
card.plain: It lights up when the text is about to say that something cannot or must not be done.
